questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of a Quotient Given the Necessary Data
questions.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

$$
f(1)=8,\,{f}^{′}(1)=6,\,g(1)=4,\,{g}^{′}(1)=4
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=1$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=1} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(1)g(1)-f(1){g}^{′}(1)}{{g}^{2}(1)} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 4-8\cdot 4}{{4}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of the Product or Quotient of a Composition of Functions Given the Necessary Data
questions.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
f(2)=-1,\,{f}^{′}(2)=-2,\,g(2)=-5,\,{g}^{′}(2)=1
$$

If $h(x)=\frac{5f(x)+4}{g(x)+6},$ find the value of ${h}^{′}(2).$
questions.worked_solution:
The quotient rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{u}{v})=\frac{v{u}^{′}-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}}.
$$

Let $u=5f(x)+4$ and $v=g(x)+6.$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={g}^{′}(x).
$$

Substituting this into the quotient rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =\frac{v{u}^{′}-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(g(x)+6)\cdot 5{f}^{′}(x)-(5f(x)+4)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x)+6)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5{f}^{′}(x)(g(x)+6)-{g}^{′}(x)(5f(x)+4)}{(g(x)+6)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

At $x=2$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(2) & =\frac{5{f}^{′}(2)(g(2)+6)-{g}^{′}(2)(5f(2)+4)}{(g(2)+6)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot (-2)\cdot (-5+6)-1\cdot (5\cdot (-1)+4)}{(-5+6)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-10)\cdot 1-(-1)}{{1}^{2}} \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=0$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $3$ | $1$ | $0$ | $2$ |

If $h(x)=\frac{3f(x)-1}{2g(x)+2},$ determine the value of ${h}^{′}(0).$
questions.worked_solution:
The quotient rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{u}{v})=\frac{v{u}^{′}-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}}.
$$

Let $u=3f(x)-1$ and $v=2g(x)+2.$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=2{g}^{′}(x).
$$

Substituting this into the quotient rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =\frac{v{u}^{′}-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(2g(x)+2)\cdot 3{f}^{′}(x)-(3f(x)-1)\cdot 2{g}^{′}(x)}{(2g(x)+2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3{f}^{′}(x)(2g(x)+2)-2{g}^{′}(x)(3f(x)-1)}{(2g(x)+2)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

At $x=0$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(0) & =\frac{3{f}^{′}(0)(2g(0)+2)-2{g}^{′}(0)(3f(0)-1)}{(2g(0)+2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 0\cdot (2\cdot 1+2)-2\cdot 2\cdot (3\cdot 3-1)}{(2\cdot 1+2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-4\cdot 8}{{4}^{2}} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=0$ are given in the table below. 

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $4$ | $-1$ | $2$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=0.$ Do not round the answer.

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=0}=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=0$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=0} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(0)g(0)-f(0){g}^{′}(0)}{(g(0))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)(4)-(\frac{1}{2})(2)}{{4}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-4-1}{16} \\  & =-\frac{5}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of a Linear Combination of Functions Given the Necessary Data
questions.problem:
The values of functions $q(x)$ and $r(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=0$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $q(x)$ | $r(x)$ | ${q}^{′}(x)$ | ${r}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $-1$ | $3$ | $2$ | $-1$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))$ at $x=0.$

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))|}_{x=0}=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))=3{q}^{′}(x)+4{r}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=0$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))|}_{x=0} & =3{q}^{′}(0)+4{r}^{′}(0) \\  & =3(2)+4(-1) \\  & =6-4 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
